deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no derivations and no handwriting by Gauss on the leaf itself. It is a printed page in Fraktur type: §1 of a German school textbook of arithmetic. Given the bundle name 'HB.Leiste', this is presumably Christian Leiste's 'Die Arithmetic und Algebra zum Gebrauch bey dem Unterrichte' (Wolfenbüttel, c. 1790). The interleaved or facing leaf carries handwritten notes, a bibliography of Euler's works, and those notes show at the left edge.

The printed text is a conventional 18th-century classification of mathematics in the Wolffian tradition.
- Mathematics is the science of magnitudes (Größen).
- Magnitudes may be considered pure (abstracted from all other properties of things) or applied. Hence there is pure and applied mathematics.
- Pure mathematics divides by subject:
  - multitude of parts gives arithmetic (Zahlenlehre, Rechenkunst);
  - extent and shape gives geometry;
  - both together, i.e. calculation of geometric magnitudes, especially triangles, gives trigonometry.
- Pure mathematics also divides by scope and method into elementary and higher mathematics (Analysis).
- Applied mathematics deals with magnitudes of the real world, in nature and in art.
  1. In nature:
     a) forces that hinder or produce motion in solid and fluid bodies, including elasticity (Schnellkraft), giving statics and mechanics;
     b) light and fire, especially light. This covers direct vision and pictures projected on a plane (optics and perspective), (β) reflection by mirrors (catoptrics), and (γ) refraction through transparent bodies (dioptrics), which continues on the next page.

The 'A' at the foot is the printer's signature mark, and 'durch=' is the catchword. There is no mathematical content to reconstruct.

results.what: Encyclopedic division of mathematics into pure/applied, arithmetic/geometry/trigonometry, elementary/higher, and applied branches (statics, mechanics, optics, perspective, catoptrics, dioptrics)
results.modern_name: Wolffian classification of the mathematical sciences (textbook preface material)
results.usually_credited_to: Christian Wolff tradition (Anfangs-Gründe aller mathematischen Wissenschaften, 1710); printed here in Leiste's textbook

deep.surprise_reason: This is a printed textbook page (Leiste's arithmetic) with standard introductory classification of mathematics. There is no mathematics and no Gauss annotation on the leaf itself; the margin script shows through from the facing handwritten page listing Euler's works.
transcription_corrections: The 'left margin, handwritten' text is not on this page. It is the right edge of the facing leaf, the handwritten bibliography of Euler's works transcribed as the previous page (e.g. 'Theoria motuum lunae ... inaequalitates ... Berol. 1753. 4', 'Constructio lentium ... Petrop. 1762. 4', 'Rostoch. 1765'). It should be dropped from this page's transcription. In particular, 't de 1763 / Euler' corresponds to 'Comete de 1769 ... Mr. L. Euler'.
In the line 'Größen, hauptsächlich der Dreyecke' the print actually shows a misprint like 'Grbßen' (inverted/damaged type). The intended reading 'Größen' is correct.
The 'A' at the bottom is the printer's signature mark and 'durch=' is the catchword (continued as 'durchsichtigen' on the next page). Neither is part of the running text.
The textbook prints 'Optic', 'Perspectiv' and 'Catoptric' (without final -k), which the transcription correctly preserves. The next page has 'Dioptrik'.
